purpose: Reuse completed taxonomy and routing; distinguish card construction from new taxonomy research. Supersedes interpretation, not source evidence, in learner-card-photo-reconciliation-20261016.json.
matching_method: Exact source name or source-row join to reviewed routing; accepted-target matching preserves rank. Canonical ID plus scientific names and synonym names screened. No new synonym or botanical identity determinations. Repeated reviews retained; old HOLD records are not blindly reinstated over later confirmed mappings.
limitations: Prior accepted-name review is not proof of specimen/photo identity, independent expert review, license clearance, completed prose, approval READY or installed card. Phase2 sheet-supported excerpts are distinguished from direct accepted-name records. Final installer duplicate/claim/photo gates remain.

separate_hold_records.name: Mimosa quadrivalvis
separate_hold_records.reason: Mimosa quadrivalvis is an accepted species in Kew, but the historical/local source concept is likely a misapplied broader North American usage; specimen/source identity must be reconciled before learner admission.

separate_hold_records.name: Onosmodium bejarense
separate_hold_records.reason: Onosmodium bejarense is likely an orthographic error for O. bejariense, but exact source identity remains unverified.

separate_hold_records.name: Schoenocaulon drummondii

separate_hold_records.reason: Kew treats Taraxacum officinale at sectional-complex level rather than a single accepted replacement species.

cautions.detail: ITIS accepts the autonym var. edwardsiana and var. petraea, whereas current POWO accepts species Anemone edwardsiana and synonymizes var. petraea; do NOT claim the autonym is an explicit POWO synonym. Source varietal identification not independently specimen-verified. No existing Anemone edwardsiana canonical card in manifest; installation is other lane's responsibility.

POWO accepts B. bracteata distinct from B. leucophaea; local Texas material historically called B. bracteata may represent B. leucophaea, so inspect source observation before attaching Texas photographs or merging.

WFO 2026 and ITIS map Hexalectris nitida to Bletia nitida (2020 combination); FNA and NatureServe may still use Hexalectris. Kew direct species record not independently retrieved; preserve familiar orchid name and concept.

Ferns of Texas explicitly treats Sceptridium biternatum as synonym of Botrychium biternatum; Kew accepted Botrychium genus lists Botrychium biternatum Underw. Regional authorship may include basionym author Savigny, requiring nomenclatural citation reconciliation; keep aliases distinct from B. dissectum.

ITIS and FNA treat Chrysopsis texana G.L.Nesom as a synonym of Bradburia hirtella. Kew POWO Chrysopsis genus accepted-species list does not include C. texana; direct POWO species record was not found. Preserve the source combination as a searchable alias and record cross-backbone caution; no observation ID or new canonical card is inferred.
